title: Naturality of the Kunneth map
statement:
Let

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X\times_SY&\xrightarrow{\;q\;}&Y\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle p}&&\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle g}\\
X&\xrightarrow{\;f\;}&S
\end{array}
$$

be a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square], set
$c=f\circ p=g\circ q$, let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, and let
$\varphi:E\to E'$ and $\psi:K\to K'$ be morphisms in
$D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$, respectively $D(Y_{\Et},\Lambda)$. Use the ordinary unbounded derived categories and derived tensor of
[def-kun-derived-tensor], and the Kunneth map of [def-kun-kunneth-map]. Then the
square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
Rf_*E\kunotimes{\Lambda}Rg_*K&\xrightarrow{\ \kappa_{E,K}\ }&
Rc_*\bigl(p^{-1}E\kunotimes{\Lambda}q^{-1}K\bigr)\\
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle Rf_*(\varphi)\otimes Rg_*(\psi)}&&
\Big\downarrow{\scriptstyle Rc_*(p^{-1}\varphi\otimes q^{-1}\psi)}\\
Rf_*E'\kunotimes{\Lambda}Rg_*K'&\xrightarrow{\ \kappa_{E',K'}\ }&
Rc_*\bigl(p^{-1}E'\kunotimes{\Lambda}q^{-1}K'\bigr)
\end{array}
$$

commutes; that is, $\kappa$ is natural in $E$ and in $K$.

proof.text: Work with the cartesian square and its chosen pullback identification from [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. Work with small representatives of the small etale sites in the larger universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] on each site with its constant sheaf of commutative rings $\Lambda_T$; this supplies the ordinary unbounded derived tensor bifunctor, denoted $\otimes^L$ below. Use the unbounded module adjunction conventions of [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] for $u=f,g,c$: each morphism $u:U\to V$ occurs as a vertical edge of the cartesian square with horizontal arrows $\mathrm{id}_U,\mathrm{id}_V$ and both vertical arrows $u$. Write $L=c^{-1}$, $R=Rc_*$ and $\eta:\mathrm{id}\to RL$. Put $M=Rf_*E\otimes^L Rg_*K$, $N=p^{-1}E\otimes^L q^{-1}K$, and use primes for the corresponding objects at $(E',K')$. Set $A=Rf_*(\varphi)\otimes^L Rg_*(\psi):M\to M'$ and $B=p^{-1}\varphi\otimes^L q^{-1}\psi:N\to N'$. By [def-kun-kunneth-map], the transpose of $\kappa_{E,K}$ is $a=d\circ\chi:LM\to N$, where $\chi:LM\xrightarrow{\sim}p^{-1}f^{-1}Rf_*E\otimes^L q^{-1}g^{-1}Rg_*K$ is its specified comparison and $d=p^{-1}\varepsilon_{f,E}\otimes^L q^{-1}\varepsilon_{g,K}$. Define $a',d',\chi'$ analogously.

source.place: Proof, fixed adjunction and the composite defining the transpose; unbounded module conventions made explicit

proof.text: Let $H=p^{-1}f^{-1}Rf_*(\varphi)\otimes^L q^{-1}g^{-1}Rg_*(\psi)$. The bifunctorial monoidality isomorphism of [lem-kun-inverse-image-monoidal], used at $c$, and the canonical identifications of inverse-image functors specified in [def-kun-kunneth-map] give $\chi'\circ L(A)=H\circ\chi$. To check the direction, put $J=c^{-1}Rf_*(\varphi)\otimes^L c^{-1}Rg_*(\psi)$ and write $m:c^{-1}Rf_*E\otimes^L c^{-1}Rg_*K\to LM$ for the canonical monoidal comparison. Its naturality equation is $L(A)\circ m=m'\circ J$; multiplication by $(m')^{-1}$ and $m^{-1}$ gives $(m')^{-1}\circ L(A)=J\circ m^{-1}$. The natural identifications $c^{-1}\cong p^{-1}f^{-1}$ and $c^{-1}\cong q^{-1}g^{-1}$ carry $J$ to $H$ and $m^{-1}$ to $\chi$, giving the claimed equation.

proof.text: The counits of the fixed unbounded adjunctions in [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] are natural transformations. Consequently $\varepsilon_{f,E'}\circ f^{-1}Rf_*(\varphi)=\varphi\circ\varepsilon_{f,E}$ and $\varepsilon_{g,K'}\circ g^{-1}Rg_*(\psi)=\psi\circ\varepsilon_{g,K}$. Applying the functors $p^{-1}$ and $q^{-1}$ gives $p^{-1}\varepsilon_{f,E'}\circ p^{-1}f^{-1}Rf_*(\varphi)=p^{-1}\varphi\circ p^{-1}\varepsilon_{f,E}$ and $q^{-1}\varepsilon_{g,K'}\circ q^{-1}g^{-1}Rg_*(\psi)=q^{-1}\psi\circ q^{-1}\varepsilon_{g,K}$. These are simply the defining naturality squares of the two counits, followed by functors.

proof.text: Use the bifunctor in [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent] to tensor the two equations of step 3. Its preservation of composition gives $d'\circ H=B\circ d$. Combining this with step 2 and the transpose formula in [def-kun-kunneth-map], associativity gives $a'\circ L(A)=d'\circ\chi'\circ L(A)=d'\circ H\circ\chi=B\circ d\circ\chi=B\circ a$. This proves the required compatibility before transposing; no assertion that a Kunneth map is invertible has been used.

source.place: Tag 06YU, definition-derived-tor and its preceding construction; composition in the derived tensor bifunctor

proof.text:
By the adjunct formula of [lem-weil-pbc-adjunct-counit-identity], the definition [def-kun-kunneth-map] gives $\kappa_{E,K}=R(a)\circ\eta_M$ and $\kappa_{E',K'}=R(a')\circ\eta_{M'}$. Naturality of the unit of $L\dashv R$ from [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] says $\eta_{M'}\circ A=RL(A)\circ\eta_M$. Thus the equation of step 4 yields
$$
\kappa_{E',K'}\circ A
=R(a')\circ\eta_{M'}\circ A
=R(a')\circ RL(A)\circ\eta_M
=R(a'\circ L(A))\circ\eta_M
=R(B\circ a)\circ\eta_M
=R(B)\circ R(a)\circ\eta_M
=R(B)\circ\kappa_{E,K}.
$$
This is exactly the stated commutative square. Taking either $\varphi$ or $\psi$ to be an identity also gives naturality in each variable separately.
